title: HEINONG65: published drought-sensitive contrast, uncalibrated engineering reference

trait_reference.scope: Published HN44/HN65 contrast supported by a flowering-stage pot experiment. Native group assignment extends that ordering to a generic whole-season water response; it is not a cultivar-calibrated field drought model.

native_response.input: native canopy ET0 and root-zone soil moisture
native_response.output: native SWEAF, critical moisture and transpiration stress RFTRA
native_response.mapping: Published tolerant/sensitive ordering assigned to native groups 5/2, respectively. Group values were chosen as an engineering contrast, not estimated from the paper.
native_response.assumption: No paper measurements are claimed to identify DEPNR, root depth, transpiration curve, field yield or all drought stages. Native SWEAF and water balance remain unchanged.

sources.title: Wang et al. (2022), Physiological Response of Soybean Plants to Water Deficit
PCSE 6 SWEAF and crop water stress source
Pinned upstream WOFOST 8.1 Soybean_901 native parameters
sources.license: EUPL as declared upstream; version unspecified

limitations: This is a complete executable native parameter set, not a published or locally validated WOFOST cultivar fit.
All non-trait parameters are copied from the pinned Northern-France Soybean_901 baseline, including thermal time, nitrogen, carbon allocation and rooting.
No conversion of active accumulated temperatures into TSUM, forced maturity, yield multiplication or harvest-gate bypass.
Quantitative trait mapping is an explicit engineering assumption; literature establishes experimental identity and ordering, not native parameter identification.
Legacy reduced-engine compatibility uses the unchanged STANDARD baseline and does not reproduce these native contrasts.
